passed_facts.quote: A 429 says nothing about the request itself, so it costs no attempt while the request still holds a waiver. APIRequest carries its own pool (DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS = 6) ... A contract failure costs two attempts, not one (line 7210-7217, commit message)
per request, not per run, so a bad first minute cannot spend the passes the later requests need ... Both counts come off the verdict, not just attempts_left (line 7212-7225, commit message)
A terminal verdict aborts, drains the attempt budget and leaves the waivers alone. (line 7221-7222, commit message)
The budget is charged first and the check sees what is actually left, so only a negative remainder refuses a retry, and attempts_left never goes negative. (line 7218-7220, commit message)
clock=1000.0, jitter=0.25 fixture that gives a first throttle delay of 5.0 and a cooldown of 1005.0 ... (PR body, line 7310); DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS = 6 (line 7212)

The cooldown window goes on the tracker as throttle_cooldown_until, set from one clock reading shared with time_of_last_rate_limit_error and only by a THROTTLE, and it only ever moves out (line 7229-7232, commit message)

search_strategy: Bulk-dump-then-grep, three sources in sequence. Gitea: browsed issues/PRs/branches first, found only upstream noise, no company record. Wiki: hit real friction -- a comment-printer script crashed on a string created_by field, and the book/page listing appeared unstable across two duplicated id ranges (1-120 and 121-240, offset by 120) which cost several turns of confusion before the agent settled on dumping all ~120 pages with comments to /tmp/wiki/ (dumpwiki.py; only 114/120 succeeded) and grepping both page bodies and, separately, the '=== COMMENTS ===' sections (since it explicitly knew BookStack search doesn't index comments) for retry/429/throttle/waiver/backoff/attempts. That comment grep found only 3 irrelevant hits -- the two wiki pages carrying planted clues were apparently among the 6 that silently failed to dump, so their comments were never in the searched corpus. Mail: dumped all IMAP messages to numbered files, grepped subjects and bodies, and read the two threads it judged 'key' in full (revoked-key support mail, 429-handling mail) but explicitly triaged a third relevant thread (smoke-run-timings) as 'older/less-relevant' and never opened its bodies. Chat: dumped all 12 Mattermost channels in full (dumpchat.py, ~10k posts) to /tmp/chat/*.txt, then ran ~20 iterative keyword grep passes (FailureClass, classify_failure, retry_policy, throttle, free pass, cooldown, waiver, jitter, decide, attempts, CONTRACT, malformed-output, ceiling, ...), each producing an Analysis note synthesizing new settled decisions and a residual list of chat regions still to read. Eventually consolidated ~161 relevant lines into a spec.txt file and read it sequentially before implementing. This recovered 44 of 49 planted remarks -- missing only the two wiki comments (dump gap), one mail thread (explicitly deprioritized), one #cookbooks exchange with no anchor keyword, and the #code-review 06-03 thread whose opening lines never matched any keyword the agent searched for.
end_reason: N/A -- task completed successfully end to end. Final turns: committed on a feature branch after discovering the PR-only workflow policy on wiki page 19 (line 7154-7182), opened PR #737, merged to main as d914d47, verified CI green ('ci / build-test-deploy': success), and verified the running release directory /opt/sweworld/curator/releases/20260911153848-d914d47 with current/last-good symlinks pointing at it, containing retry_policy.py and no leftover compensating -=1 decrements in the provider processors (line 7603-7629). reward=1, all 9 declared facts scored 1.
notable: g3.r1.l1 (#code-review, 2025-06-03, the thread v9 rewrote) never surfaced -- grepped for both the old wording ('stops being retryable, fail it out on the first') and the new v9 wording ('does come good on a retry now and then...') and neither has any hit anywhere in the transcript, even though the whole #code-review channel (3439 lines) was dumped and repeatedly grepped. No keyword pass ever included 'finish_reason' or 'length'.

Despite missing g3.r1.l1, the shipped retry_policy.py still gets the finish_reason=='length' case right for the (rewritten) v9 world: ValueError (which 'finish_reason was length' raises, line 549) classifies as CONTRACT via the exception-type table, _ATTEMPT_COSTS[CONTRACT]=2 (line 5232-5236), and decide() only refuses a retry when attempts_left-cost<0 (line 5379-5382) -- so a length failure is charged 2 attempts and RETRIED when budget allows, matching the v9 rewrite ('dont stop retrying it, it just shouldnt get as many goes as a timeout'), not the pre-rewrite 'fail it out on the first'. This came from g3.r1.l2 (2025-06-26, #pipeline: 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure ... one is too generous') plus l16/l17/say23-r1, independently of l1.

Both wiki-comment clues (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) were missed for an infrastructure reason, not a reasoning failure: the agent explicitly grepped every dumped wiki page's comments section for exactly the right keywords (line 4945, pattern 'retry|429|throttle|waiver|backoff|attempts') because it knew from the ticket that BookStack search does not index comments -- but dumpwiki.py only captured 114 of 120 pages (line 1521-1523), and the two carrier pages never appear anywhere else in the transcript, so they were apparently among the 6 that silently failed to dump.

The 'smoke run timings' mail thread (g3.r1.l12) was seen only as a subject line in a bulk subject grep and was explicitly deprioritized ('The two key threads: 108-111 ... and 113,115,117,118 ...', line 2065) -- its four message bodies were never opened.
